new_categories.label: shutdown_link_interface_readiness
new_categories.memory: The delivered ship/shore protective link/interface can be represented as a service-state distinct from cargo-transfer machinery or normal valve-control readiness.

new_categories.label: ship_endpoint_readiness
new_categories.memory: The ship-side endpoint can have its own readiness and degradation state without inferring signal type, trip logic or shutdown action.

new_categories.label: shore_endpoint_readiness
new_categories.memory: The shore-side endpoint can be modeled separately from the ship endpoint and from terminal-wide cargo-transfer readiness.

new_categories.label: inter_endpoint_link_path_availability
new_categories.memory: The bounded connection/path between ship and shore endpoints can be available, degraded, isolated or restored independently of endpoint hardware state.

new_categories.label: non_operational_signal_indication_confidence
new_categories.memory: A non-operational confidence state can represent whether link status/indication is trustworthy without retaining actual signal values, test methods or response sequences.

new_categories.label: independence_support_confidence
new_categories.memory: Confidence in protective independence/support should remain distinct from mere shared power/control availability and from proof of any exact fail-safe design.

new_categories.label: terminal_interface_scope
new_categories.memory: Readiness can be scoped to the particular ship/shore terminal interface rather than generalized to all terminal or vessel cargo operations.

new_categories.label: transfer_operation_scope_localization
new_categories.memory: A restriction can be localized to the affected transfer/interface scope without inferring whole-vessel or whole-terminal unavailability.

new_categories.label: endpoint_link_redundancy_confidence
new_categories.memory: Redundancy or alternate-interface confidence can be represented abstractly without inferring approved changeover, bypass or substitution procedures.

new_categories.label: protective_link_degradation_lifecycle
new_categories.memory: The service can move through available, degraded, restricted, isolated, under-verification and restored states while retaining timestamps for each transition.

new_categories.label: scoped_restriction_and_isolation
new_categories.memory: Restriction/isolation can be attributed separately to link path, ship endpoint, shore endpoint, indication domain, support dependency or terminal interface.

new_categories.label: downstream_effect_not_root_cause_proof
new_categories.memory: Cargo-transfer restriction, terminal incompatibility, protective-assurance loss, rework or schedule effect should not by itself prove which endpoint, link, indication or support layer caused degradation.

new_categories.label: multi_timestamp_restoration_verification
new_categories.memory: Physical repair, link availability, indication confidence, interface acceptance and operational release can occur at different times and should not be collapsed into one restoration timestamp.

useful_refinements.label: overfill_protection_vs_ship_shore_link
useful_refinements.memory: P096-style tank high-level/overfill assurance is a different protective function from ship/shore shutdown-link interface readiness even when downstream transfer restrictions overlap.

useful_refinements.label: normal_valve_actuation_vs_shutdown_link
useful_refinements.memory: P100-style normal remote cargo-valve actuation/control readiness does not establish readiness of a separate ship/shore emergency-shutdown communication/interface layer.

useful_refinements.label: terminal_vapor_interface_vs_shutdown_link
useful_refinements.memory: A terminal-interface concept from vapor-control service refines scope handling but does not duplicate the protective shutdown-link service.

useful_refinements.label: utility_control_support_vs_delivered_protective_link
useful_refinements.memory: Electrical/control support can be an upstream dependency while the delivered protective link/interface remains a separate service-state confidence domain.

duplicates.label: generic_protective_service_state_lifecycle
duplicates.memory: Generic available/degraded/restricted/isolated/restored lifecycle mechanics are already represented across prior protective-service families.

duplicates.label: generic_scoped_degradation_and_restoration
duplicates.memory: Generic scope-localization, downstream-effect separation and verified-restoration mechanics are repeated campaign-wide rather than unique to this family.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: exact signal media or signal types
exact trip logic, shutdown actions or interlocks
exact response timing, test values or operating sequences
negative_space: exact ship/shore shutdown-link arrangements, endpoint topology, signal types, trip logic, shutdown actions, interlocks, response timing, test values and current configuration
exact shutdown-link testing, connection, arming, transfer coordination, bypass, reset, troubleshooting, emergency-response or operating procedures
named shutdown-link providers, terminals, inspectors, incidents, deficiency findings and current readiness
private or regional terminal/link equipment and support lineages plus non-English predecessor terminology
stop_reason: The bounded structural questions are answered; further recall trends toward exact signal, trip, shutdown, interlock, timing, test, procedure, provider or incident detail that is deferred to Evidence.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only defensive ship/shore shutdown-link service-state orientation and source-discovery output; not shutdown, trip, bypass, testing, cargo-transfer or emergency-response operating advice and not proof of any exact arrangement, signal, action, interlock, timing, procedure, provider, incident or current-readiness fact.
